question: Which reactions and concrete measures have been adopted by the Commission, the VicePresident of the Commission / High Representative of the Union for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy and the European External Action Service in response to the public statements made by the President of Burundi, Évariste Ndayishimiye, on 29 December 2023, in which he called for the public stoning of homosexuals?

How does the Commission judge the public statements of the Burundian President in light of the decision to resume development cooperation with Burundi only two years ago, after the EU had suspended all direct funding to the Burundian Government in 2016 because of its disregard for human rights and its failure to stop a wave of deadly violence?
Is the Commission planning to critically review development cooperation with Burundi, both with regard to the level of funding and to the channels of cooperation? If so, how, and if not, why not?
answer: The European External Action Service conveyed the EU’s grave concerns on these remarks to the Burundian Ambassador to the EU and the Minister of Interior and Minister of Justice in Bujumbura. It reiterated the importance of the respect of human rights and freedoms for all and the key part this plays in bilateral relations with Burundi.

While the authorities reiterated their legal and cultural negative stance on same sex relationship, they also stressed that the President’s remarks were to be treated as a figure of speech. No specific action or campaign against homosexuals appears to have been launched following the remarks in question.

In February 2022, the EU repealed the 2016 decision that suspended its direct financial assistance to the Burundian administration, in accordance with Council Decision 2016/394 (1) of 14 March 2016. The repeal was motivated by the acknowledgment of some progress since the 2020 election and a new phase in the EU-Burundi relations.

The EU remains committed to advancing human rights and continues closely monitoring developments in Burundi and regionally. Budget support is not currently disbursed. The EU is engaged in a Mid-Term Review of the Multi-Annual Financial Framework 2021-2027, which will have an impact on funds disbursed for international partnerships.

As a result of this assessment, the Multiannual Indicative Programmes for partner countries may be amended. The EU’s cooperation with Burundi will remain in line with the EU Global Gateway strategy (2) and the EU Gender Action Plan III.
